exam: 1984 AP Chemistry MCQ · Version indicated in source
text:
38.  The radioactive decay of 146 C to 147 N occurs by the
     process of

    A)  beta particle emission
    B)  alpha particle emission
    C)  positron emission
    D)  electron capture
    E)  neutron capture

candidates.name: Spectroscopy and molecular transitions
candidates.definition: Matching regions of the electromagnetic spectrum to the molecular changes they cause: microwave to rotation, infrared to vibration, and UV-visible to electronic transitions.
candidates.include: Tag when a type of radiation must be linked to the transition it causes, or absorption versus emission distinguished.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag photon energy calculations (tag photon-energy) or PES (tag photoelectron-spectroscopy).

candidates.name: Nuclear chemistry
candidates.definition: Radioactive decay modes, nuclear equations and nuclear binding energy. Not assessed on the current AP Chemistry exam (first-order half-life math belongs to integrated-rate-laws).
candidates.include: Tag legacy questions about decay particles, nuclear equations or transmutation.
candidates.exclude: Do not tag first-order kinetics problems that merely use radioactive decay as context unless nuclear equations are required.
